oil.summary: Crude staged a sharp reversal Monday, with WTI shedding 5.63% to $80.00/bbl and Brent dropping 6.51% to $84.29, unwinding a portion of the prior month's near 17% rally. The catalyst was Trump's decision to call off a planned attack on Iranian energy sites, deflating the geopolitical risk premium that had built on Iran's Strait of Hormuz blockade of Gulf neighbors' exports. Compounding the bearish impulse, Kuwait's July output surged to 1.971 mb/d as OPEC+ completed its cut reversal — options markets now price a 77% probability of a further OPEC production decrease at the next meeting, suggesting the market doubts the group can defend price levels. Supply-route stress persists nonetheless: dark tanker transits at Bab el-Mandeb are rising as Houthi threats on Saudi Red Sea shipments continue, and Ukraine struck three Russian refineries over the weekend.
drivers: Trump cancels planned strike on Iranian energy infrastructure, collapsing the Hormuz risk premium and triggering broad crude sell-off
Kuwait output hits 1.971 mb/d in July as OPEC+ fully unwinds prior production cuts, adding supply-side pressure
Red Sea / Bab el-Mandeb disruption and Ukraine strikes on Russian refineries limit the downside, but insufficient to offset Iran headline relief

gas.summary: European gas diverged sharply from the month-long trend today: TTF fell 2.06% to €57.855/MWh after Trump signalled he had called off an attack on Iranian energy sites, reducing the tail risk of a broader Middle East supply shock. That same Iran relief trade drove the move. A Greek-owned LNG carrier was involved in an incident in the Strait of Hormuz at end of last week but cleared safely, a reminder that Hormuz transit risk remains live even as headline tensions ease. Henry Hub was broadly flat, edging up just 0.66% to $2.765/MMBtu with no domestic catalysts in today's headlines; its one-month decline of 13.49% reflects a distinctly looser US supply-demand picture than Europe's. Australian regulators proposed tighter pollution rules for the Santos- and Inpex-led Darwin LNG plants, a longer-term cost consideration.
drivers: Trump's Iran de-escalation signal triggers sharp TTF sell-off, reversing part of the month-long geopolitical risk build-up
Greek LNG tanker incident in the Strait of Hormuz highlights residual Hormuz transit risk despite today's price relief
Henry Hub near-flat on no fresh domestic catalysts; US and European gas markets continue to diverge on fundamentals

power.summary: EU Carbon EUAs edged down 0.82% to $76.38/EUA, a relatively muted move consistent with the broader risk-off tone but cushioned by the month's near-flat carbon price trajectory. TTF's 2% decline today matters for power pricing given gas-fired generation's role in marginal price setting across European grids. A drone attack on the UAE nuclear power plant was reported, adding a security dimension to non-fossil baseload, though the headline's supply impact on European carbon markets is indirect. Shell agreed to sell its European onshore renewables portfolio to TotalEnergies, a notable asset reshuffle among majors. India announced potential transmission charge waivers to rescue stalled solar and wind projects, a supportive policy signal for renewables build-out. Trump's mixed messaging on Iran — simultaneously winding down conflict and adding troops — keeps the geopolitical backdrop uncertain for energy infrastructure broadly.
drivers: TTF decline weighs on European power marginal costs and reduces near-term EUA demand pressure from gas-to-power switching
Shell sells European onshore renewables portfolio to TotalEnergies, signalling continued portfolio reshaping among oil majors
Drone attack on UAE nuclear plant and ongoing Iran uncertainty maintain geopolitical risk for power infrastructure despite today's partial de-escalation
